descriptionHtml:
Approach · TC-20 Rounding Dashboard · S20a Web: a browser with the wrong date and another time zone shows the same counts and In Today set (3.8)

UAT steps / ticket ACs covered:

  • T4 'In Today' attendance is kept per day by the server clock, so the dashboard counts follow each server day's attendance. A device with a wrong clock or another time zone shows the same counts (TFA-92587 AC 6; UAT 3.8)

Test design technique: Device (device) — Look at the layout and gestures at phone size or on a real device (iPhone / Pixel).

Given The standard fixture account, resident In Today. Two browser contexts on the same account: A normal; B with timezoneId 'Pacific/Honolulu' and page.clock set one day ahead

When Open both dashboards and the Nursing Home Today's Visits list in both contexts

Then Identical counts, rows and In Today residents in both contexts. Each context's date line is recorded against the server day (Q4)

Pass rule (oracle, excerpt): UAT 3.8 (same state on any device) and TFA-92587 AC 6 (server time). Counts, rows and the Today's Visits list must be identical between the two contexts. The date line is recorded and judged after Q4 (on main it comes from new Date() in RoundingDashboard.tsx, so B shows a different date). reqs is T4 alone (ungated), so a difference reports as a Fail

Where it ran: local newspec-c (new Playwright specs); test method PW · Playwright script; lane planned in the matrix: existing tests (Tim's Playwright) (blocked)

S20a is our own case number (its number in the coverage matrix cases/TC-20.matrix.json; a letter suffix = one case split in several), not a step number of the UAT document.

Environment: local — main e02167f, local stack (not a deployed build); run folder runs/2026-10-14-local, lane newspec-c.

Test method: PW · Playwright script; secondary: MULTI · Multi-device / multi-account — as classified in cases/test-methods.json, which says it runs on both; Source: newspec-c.

UAT item: TC-20 Rounding Dashboard · Section: A5 · Cross-Cutting · Scenario: TC-20/S20a

Web: a browser with the wrong date and another time zone shows the same counts and In Today set (3.8)

Tickets: TFA-92587 All Residents Attendance Toggle (ready for qa)

New local lane newspec-c: status passed in newspec-c/results.json → passed (passed).

How it is tested (newspec-c/plan.json, automatable: yes): New Playwright spec: fresh account seeded with Hospital patients (pending, pre-rounded, note-ready, post-rounded) and Nursing Home residents (In Today pending, In Today pre-rounded, not In Today complete). Context A normal; context B timezoneId Pacific/Honolulu, clock +1 day. Read both dashboards (counts, rows + badges) and the Nursing Home Today's Visits list on both; compare A vs B and against the server rows. Record each context's date line against the server day (Q4, record-only). Today's Visits is read after a known In Today row shows and two reads 500 ms apart agree (no fixed wait). — Two contexts, clock and timezone are Playwright features; the counts are DOM reads.

Detail:

Re-run 16:54 JST after review: 15/15 judged checks pass on the first attempt: counts, rows/badges and Today's Visits identical on A (Tokyo, real clock) and B (Honolulu), for B = +24 h (same calendar date as A at this hour) and B = next calendar day; B's visit changed nothing A sees. Flaky first attempt noted: in the earlier all-specs run (final/run-all.log, reports/all.json retry 0) the first attempt failed because A's Today's Visits read came back empty after a fixed 1.5 s wait; the retry passed. Fixed in the spec: Today's Visits is read after a known In Today row shows and two reads 500 ms apart agree. Record-only: B's dashboard date line follows the device ('Thursday, October 15' vs server/host Wednesday Oct 14, Q4); B's device day rolled a same-day New Admission to Follow-up dated 2026-10-15 for everyone (known TFA-92584); B's stored 12 h session was dropped as expired by its own clock (signing in again worked).

Evidence: 3 attached.

This local result replaces that dev entry (the scenario appears once).
